one_line_contribution: A task-type provenance crossover in ALFWorld that labels a retrieved memory bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction by the episodes that built each, and reports as a scale-free ratio with a CI the fraction of the bank's task-type-specific advantage that the same-episode instruction already holds.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144) threatens novelty more than the proposal admits. ExpeL runs on ALFWorld, distills training episodes into a natural-language insights block prepended to the prompt, AND retrieves successful trajectories — and its own ablation removes the insight container and the retrieval container separately on the same training pool. That is the two-container comparison, in this exact environment, from the same episodes. The proposal cites ExpeL only for the framing concession ('memory as an instruction is not a framing we invented') and never engages with that ablation table; a reviewer who knows ExpeL will ask why the paper's Related Work treats it as a design-pattern precedent rather than as the nearest published measurement. Behind it, EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) supplies the qualitative headline (ReasoningBank +3.6 vs GEPA +1.2 on shared trajectories), MIPROv2 (2406.11695) the instruction-vs-demonstration split, and AutoManual (2405.16247) / AutoGuide (2403.08978) the compile-ALFWorld-experience-into-instruction-text result. What genuinely survives is narrow: provenance labelling of both containers and the interaction it identifies, the episode-disjoint controls, and a number with an interval. The proposal says this itself, and its self-assessed ceiling ('identification-and-quantification on top of an accepted qualitative claim') is the right one.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory estimand does not test the title, and can pass while the title's claim is false. A and A0 are built on Inner(I) = acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x B_oth), which isolates only the TYPE-SPECIFIC slice of the bank's value. Nothing in Inner touches the type-generic component. So A = 1.0 -- the instruction holds every scrap of type-specific content -- is fully compatible with the bank still adding 5+ points over no-memory at I_own, because the generic component was never in the numerator or the denominator. The proposal concedes the possibility in refutation route (vii), yet the bar is 'A and A0 only; nothing else gates the confirmatory claim', and the quantity that would decide the title, g(I_all, B_all), sits at n=800 under a +/-3pt TOST the proposal itself says is declarable 'only when the observed effect is within ~0.2pt of zero'. A paper can therefore report a passing absorbed share of 0.6 next to a real, unrefuted 4pt residual memory gain, and the answer to 'Is Your Agent's Memory Just an Un-Optimized Prompt?' is no. Second, and concretely: the co-primary A0 is presented as the neutral denominator but has the LARGEST headroom bias of the three, and that bias is never computed. G2 fixes acc(I_own x M0) - acc(I0* x M0) >= 3pt and the design expects a ~5pt gain from I0* to I_oth, so the I0*-to-I_own level gap is roughly 8-11pt; at the planned ~50% accuracy A_h(A0) = (l_own - l_0)/(1 - l_0) = 0.16-0.22, i.e. at or above the 0.2 lower-bound floor A0 must clear. Prediction 3's 'A_h <= 0.15' is defined only for the A denominator (l_own - l_oth)/(1 - l_oth), and the claim that the null replicates 'price the headroom floor into the decision' fails for A0 specifically, because the ladder-level null is computed between two ADJACENT Ladder-T rungs -- a small level gap -- not across the much larger I0*-to-I_own gap that A0 actually spans. The intersection-union test thus swaps a mis-specification bias for an uncomputed headroom bias, and the two endpoints share a numerator, so a numerator artifact moves both (risk 25 concedes exactly this).
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, none expensive. (1) Make the title's claim the confirmatory claim: promote g(I_own, B_own) = acc(I_own x B_own) - acc(I_own x M0) to the confirmatory family at n=1,200 (it is already free from rows 2 and 3), and pre-register the conjunction -- absorbed share above threshold AND residual memory gain equivalent to zero -- as the only outcome that supports 'memory is an un-optimized prompt'. A high A with a surviving memory gain should be pre-declared a 'type-specific content absorbed, generic content not' finding, with a different title, rather than a pass. (2) Compute and pre-register A_h separately for each of the three denominators, and add a null replicate that instantiates the I0*-to-I_own level gap (A between two instructions of that gap with no provenance difference), instead of relying on an adjacent-rung ladder null whose true value is a much smaller floor. (3) Take the frontier reflector the track budget explicitly offers (a few hundred dollars; the proposal costs its own reflection role at ~4,000 calls). The refusal is self-imposed, it makes G2 a 'live risk' by the proposal's own admission, and since a weaker reflector lowers A, it simultaneously biases toward the null AND shrinks the level gap the design is fighting -- taking the API removes the optimizer-failure branch and raises the chance G3's 9pt Inner is reachable at all. (4) Move R_raw / M_all read at I_own into Tier 0 and off the cut list.
missing_baseline: Two. First and most damaging: the plain memory-vs-no-memory delta at the own-type optimized instruction, g(I_own, B_own) = acc(I_own x B_own) - acc(I_own x M0). It is computable for free from Tier-0 rows 2 and 3 at n=1,200, it is the quantity every memory paper the proposal cites actually reports, and it is thresholded nowhere, predicted nowhere, and absent from the confirmatory family -- while its weaker n=800 pooled cousin g(I_all, B_all) carries the entire deployment claim under a TOST margin the proposal admits is barely declarable. Second: the whole-bank long-context dump read at the optimized instruction (R_raw / M_all at I_own). EvoMemBench (2605.18421), which the proposal itself cites, reports long-context baselines staying competitive with fifteen memory methods; if simply pasting the bank at I_own matches retrieval, the container framing is about retrieval overhead rather than about instructions absorbing episodes. That arm is Tier 1 and fourth on the contingency cut list, i.e. likely never run.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually serious for a proposal -- dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 queries over 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, one competitor PDF read in full with a committed SHA256, a self-correction of a web snippet that misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6, and reinstatement of five IDs wrongly retracted in an earlier version. I credit that. But it does not establish novelty, for reasons the document itself supplies. All four pre-freeze obligations are declared UNRUN, including the freeze-blocking search of the contamination and data-attribution literatures for the provenance-crossover primitive on which the entire identification claim rests, and the named live collision -- the unopened appendix of arXiv 2608.14036 -- that would gut prediction 6. More telling than the unrun items is the scan's demonstrated failure mode: weighting to the last six months caused it to miss AutoManual (2405.16247, NeurIPS 2024) and AutoGuide (2403.08978), the two most on-point papers, in this exact environment, and they were supplied by a reviewer rather than found by the scan. A search process that has already missed the two nearest precedents once is evidence against the residual novelty claim, not neutral. Verification depth is also uneven: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every 2026 ID except EvoAgentBench rests on a single web-snippet channel, and every 'confirmed absent from the paper' claim about a competitor other than EvoAgentBench is asserted from an abstract. On my own knowledge, the pre-cutoff IDs the argument leans on -- ExpeL 2308.10144, GEPA 2507.19457, MIPROv2 2406.11695, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, AutoManual, AutoGuide -- are real and accurately characterized, which is a genuine credibility signal for the unverifiable 2026 set. The collision the check misses is not a recent preprint at all: ExpeL's own ALFWorld ablation already separates a distilled-insight container from a retrieved-trajectory container built from the same training pool, and the check never treats it as a collision.
